samples.question: The picture shows a plain background, one thin vertical grey rule, and a number of identical solid dots, all the same size and the same colour. Every dot lies either fully to the left of the grey rule or fully to the right of it, and the two sides always hold the same number of dots. The dots on the right side were produced from the dots on the left side by exactly one of two operations, and by nothing else: either every left dot was reflected across the grey rule, as in a mirror, or the whole left group was slid sideways to the right without being flipped, keeping every dot at its own height. Under both operations each dot keeps its vertical position, the two groups hold the same number of dots, cover the same total area of ink, span the same width and height, and have the same average position, so dot colour, dot size, dot count, ink, group width and group centre never indicate which operation was used. Only the arrangement of the right dots relative to one another decides it: under the mirror the left-to-right order of the dots is turned around, and under the slide it is kept. Which operation produced the right group: mirror or copy? Answer with exactly one word, "mirror" or "copy".
